Hi Soojin — attaching our third-pass redlines to the MSA. A couple of items we want to surface up-front so your legal team can advise: 

1) We notice Redwood's standard Liability cap excludes (or doesn't explicitly include) pass-through claims from third-party OSS licensors (e.g., GPL, Apache obligations). Our counsel wants clarity that any claim we pass through for OSS compliance or licensing breaches will be actionable and not absorbed by an overly broad limitation.

2) Related: carve-outs for willful misconduct and IP indemnity — can you confirm Redwood's position on whether OSS-originating copyright claims are covered under your IP indemnity? If not, is a pass-through with a separate cap acceptable?

3) Order Form impact: we plan to request a line in the order form that lists any accepted carve-outs (so procurement can route for approval).

We flagged the key pages in the redline. Happy to hop on a call with your counsel next week.

Marcus / Soojin — thanks for the clear flags. I reviewed DataFoundry's redlines and Redwood's standard MSA. Below are two options we can propose (we prefer Option A for risk control but provide Option B as a middle ground). Please review and let me know which you'd like to present back.

Option A (preferred — limited pass-through for copyright only):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section X (Limitation of Liability) or the IP Indemnity clause, Redwood will be liable for, and will indemnify Customer for, direct third-party copyright infringement claims that arise solely from Redwood's distribution of third-party open-source software or model artifacts where Redwood's distribution materially altered the original licensed artifact and caused the infringement. Such pass-through indemnity shall be subject to a separate cap equal to the greater of (i) $250,000 or (ii) the total fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months. This pass-through remedy is available only upon Customer providing (a) prompt written notice, (b) sole control to Redwood of the defense and settlement, and (c) cooperation in Redwood's defense."
Rationale: narrows exposure to copyright claims, excludes general OSS compliance obligations (e.g., source distribution, attribution) and keeps cap proportional to spend.

Option B (compromise — broader but higher cap):
"Redwood will accept pass-through liability for third-party claims arising from the use or distribution of open-source software incorporated by Redwood into the Service, excluding obligations that would require Customer to distribute Customer's own source code. The pass-through cap shall be the greater of (i) $1,000,000 or (ii) the total fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months."
Practical notes: 
- We cannot accept open-ended pass-through for indemnity obligations that would require us to remediate Customer's own license compliance (Customer has primary responsibility for its own combination and redistribution decisions).
- If DataFoundry needs a broader pass-through, we should expect higher cap or a carve-out in the order form for insurance review / exec approval.

I've attached a short draft doc with the language (redwood-proposed-oss-exclusion.docx). If helpful, we can try to fold the agreed text into the Order Form's Special Terms section so procurement has a clear line item.
